questions: If the file already contains JSON lines from previous runs, should the new JSON line be appended even if it creates a file that is not a valid JSON document overall (i.e., a series of JSON objects separated by newlines)?
Should the function create the file (and any necessary directories) if it does not exist, or should it assume the file path is writable and raise an error if the directory doesn't exist?
What encoding should be used for reading the existing file content when appending? The clarification only mentions compact JSON, but not file encoding for the append operation.
If the URL returns a non-HTML content type (e.g., plain text, XML, or a binary file), should the function still attempt to parse it with BeautifulSoup, or should it handle it as having no title?
Should the function follow HTTP redirects automatically (as requests.get does by default), or should it treat the final URL after redirects as the source for the title?
What should happen if the title tag exists but is empty (e.g., <title></title>)? Should it be saved as an empty string or as None?
Is the function required to close the file explicitly after writing, or is it acceptable to rely on the context manager or garbage collection?
Should the function validate the URL format (e.g., ensure it starts with http:// or https://) before making the request, or delegate all validation to requests.get?
